findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the database a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than keeping it private inside the VPC. Combined with the exported catalog_db_endpoint output, this materially widens the attack surface of the data tier.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and snapshots, leaving stored application data in cleartext at the storage layer.

The master password is supplied from var.password and the same value is interpolated into EC2 user_data, so the credential is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state rather than being sourced from a secrets manager; the instance also uses the predictable privileged username 'admin'.

findings.issue_category: no enforced TLS for DB connections
findings.description: The attached parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport, and the generated PHP client calls mysqli_connect without TLS options, so credentials and query data can traverse the network in cleartext.

The user_data script writes the database username and master password (var.password) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service by any process or compromised application on the host, and is visible via the EC2 API and in Terraform state.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an instance carrying a highly privileged instance profile; an SSRF or injection flaw in the hosted PHP application could be used to steal the role's credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the root volume, which holds the plaintext database credential file written by user_data, may be unencrypted at rest.

The instance's public DNS is exported as an output, indicating it receives a public IP and serves the PHP application over plain HTTP (httpd with no TLS configuration) with no load balancer or TLS termination, so form submissions travel in cleartext.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by an internet-facing web server. Compromise of the PHP application yields account-wide control of S3 data, EC2 (including security-group and instance-profile manipulation, a privilege-escalation path) and all RDS instances.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application tier's security group, so any host in any subnet of the VPC can reach the database directly, defeating tier segmentation.
